####################################################################################################
Purpose of script: This script creates a list of model formulas for each pathogen to be used with 
Bayesian regression models (BRMS). It handles both univariate (uni-pathogen) and multivariate
(uni-pathogen and multi-pathogen) model specifications.

Functions Used:
- `fun_formula_add.R`: Function to add new expression to list making sure it did not exist and the 
name is not repeated
- `fun_formula.R` and helper `fun_formula_multipathogen`: Function to generate BRMS formulas.

Outputs: 
For each unipathogen, multi-unipathogen and multi-multipathogen (46), in the folder 
outputs/modfit:
- `formula_brms_{i}_l.rds` 
####################################################################################################

# Load packages, themes, directories, and functions
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
source("../00_pck.R")
source("../00_dirs.R")
source("../fun_mod/fun_formula_add.R")
source("../fun_mod/fun_formula.R")
```

# Read in the data
```{r}
dat_l <- lapply(str_subset(list.files(glue("{dirs$modfit}"), full.names = TRUE), "s08.rds"), readRDS)
names(dat_l) <- sub(".*brms_(.*?)_(vl|v1|v3)_s08.*", "\\1", 
                    str_subset(list.files(glue("{dirs$modfit}")), "s08.rds"))
``` 

# For univariate models, quality checks on factor levels and grouping variables to define covariates
```{r}
# Verify that each pathogen (pat) and vaccine name (vac_name_v1) combination has multiple levels of 
# vaccine concentration (vac_conc).
bind_rows(dat_l[str_subset(names(dat_l), "multi", negate = TRUE)], .id = "pat") %>%
  distinct(pat, vac_name_v1, vac_conc) %>%
  group_by(pat, vac_name_v1) %>%
  summarise(tot_conc = n(), .groups = "drop") 

# Count the number of unique countries per region (reg_6) for each pathogen.
# Note: For HAV and polio OPV, country-level grouping is not applicable.
bind_rows(dat_l, .id = "pat") %>%
  distinct(pat, reg_6, country) %>%
  group_by(pat, reg_6) %>%
  summarise(tot_country = n()) %>%
  group_by(pat) %>%
  summarise(max(tot_country), .groups = "drop")
# Count the number of unique studies per region (reg_6) for each pathogen.
# Note: For HAV and polio OPV, study-level grouping is not applicable.
bind_rows(dat_l, .id = "pat") %>%
  distinct(pat, reg_6, study) %>%
  group_by(pat, reg_6) %>%
  summarise(tot_study = n()) %>%
  group_by(pat) %>%
  summarise(max(tot_study), .groups = "drop")
```

# Define the univariate models dataframe 
```{r}
# Create a data frame 'patuni_df' that specifies:
# - The pathogen identifier ('pat').
# - The dosing scheme ('doses'), which differentiates between one-dose ("d1") and multi-dose ("d3")
# models.
# - Additional covariates ('others') to be included in the model, defined based on the pathogen type.

patuni_df <- data.frame(
  pat = c("rota", "vzv", "measl", "mumps", "rubel", "hav", "hbv", "hib", "mena", "menc", "meny",  
          "ipv1", "ipv2", "ipv3", "opv1", "opv2", "opv3", "dipht", "tetan", "pertuwpt", 
          "pertuapt", "pertuafha", "pertuaprn",
          "strep01", "strep03", "strep04", "strep05", "strep06a", "strep06b", "strep07f", 
          "strep09v", "strep14", "strep18c", "strep19a", "strep19f", "strep23f")) %>%
  mutate(
    doses = case_when(pat %in% c("vzv", "measl", "mumps", "rubel", "hav") ~ "d1", TRUE ~ "d3"),
    others = case_when(
      # Pathogens with different vaccine names and concentrations
      pat %in% c("dipht", "tetan", "strep01", "strep03", "strep04", "strep05", "strep06a", "strep06b", 
                 "strep07f", "strep09v", "strep14", "strep18c", "strep19a", "strep19f", "strep23f") ~ 
        list(c("vac_conc", "vac_name_v1", "(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      # Pathogens with different vaccine concentrations only 
      pat %in% c("vzv", "measl", "mumps", "rubel", "mena", "menc", "meny", "hib", 
                 "pertuwpt", "pertuapt", "pertuafha", "pertuaprn") ~ 
        list(c("vac_conc", "(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      # Pathogens with same vaccine and concentration in all studies:
      pat %in% c("hbv", "ipv1", "ipv2", "ipv3") ~ 
        list(c("(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      pat %in% c("hav", "opv1", "opv2", "opv3") ~ 
        list(c("(1|center)", "(1|center:rct_group)")),
      pat == "rota" ~ 
        list(c("doses", "vac_conc", "(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      TRUE ~ list(NULL)))
```

# For multivariate models, quality checks on factor levels and grouping variables to define covariates
```{r}
# Verify that each pathogen (pat) and vaccine name (vac_name_v1) combination has multiple levels of 
# vaccine concentration (vac_conc).
bind_rows(dat_l[str_subset(names(dat_l), "multi")], .id = "pat") %>%
  distinct(pat, vac_name_v1, vac_conc) %>%
  group_by(pat, vac_name_v1) %>%
  summarise(tot_conc = n(), .groups = "drop") 
```

# Define the multivariate models dataframe 
```{r}
# Create a data frame 'patmulti_df' for multivariate models that specifies:
# - The pathogen identifier ('pat').
# - The dosing scheme ('doses').
# - Additional covariates ('others') specific to multivariate models.
# - The 'multi_pat' column, which extracts the multiple response variable names from the
# corresponding data file

patmulti_df <- data.frame(
  pat = c("multi_men", "multi_ipv", "multi_opv", "multi_pertua",
          "multi_strep7", "multi_strep10", "multi_strep11", "multi_strep13", 
          "multi_dtpa", "multi_dtpw", "multi_hib-men", "multi_mmr", "multi_mmr-vzv")) %>%
  mutate(
    doses = case_when(pat %in% c("multi_mmr-vzv", "multi_mmr") ~ "d1", TRUE ~ "d3"),
    others = case_when(
      # Pathogens with different vaccine names and concentrations
      #### Taking out last level as rct_group not convering 
      pat %in% c("multi_strep10") ~ list(
        c("(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center)")),
      pat %in% c("multi_strep11") ~ list(
        c("vac_conc", "(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      # Pathogens with different vaccine concentrations only 
      pat %in% c("multi_men", "multi_pertua") ~ list(
        c("vac_conc", "(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      # Pathogens with same vaccine and concentration in all studies:
      pat %in% c("multi_ipv", "multi_mmr", "multi_mmr-vzv", "multi_dtpw") ~ 
        list(c("(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
      #### Taking out last level as rct_group not convering 
      pat %in% c("multi_dtpa", "multi_hib-men", "multi_opv", "multi_strep13", "multi_strep7") ~ 
        list(c("(1|study)")),
      TRUE ~ list(NULL))) %>%
  rowwise() %>%  # Ensure operations happen row by row
  mutate(multi_pat = list(readRDS(glue(
    "{dirs$modfit}/data_brms_{pat}_{case_when(doses == 'd1' ~ 'v1', .default = 'v3')}_s08.rds")) %>%
      names() %>%
      str_subset("imm_val_s1") %>%
      str_remove("imm_val_s1_"))) %>%
  ungroup()
```

# Formulas for photoperiod models ==================================================================

# Define variables and model configurations specific to photoperiod models
```{r}
# Define cluster variable names
cluster_varnames <- c("reg_6", "reg_4", "reg_3", "reg_2")

# Create a grid of model names and corresponding region variable names. This includes:
# - "csi": A model incorporating interaction with region.
# - "base" and "cs": Models without region interactions.
mod_photo_df <- expand_grid(
  model_nm = c("csi"),
  varname = c("reg_6", "reg_4", "reg_3", "reg_2")
) %>%
  add_row(model_nm = "base", varname = "") %>%
  add_row(model_nm = "cs", varname = "") %>%
  arrange(model_nm)

# Combine Pathogen Data with Photoperiod Model Configurations:
# Generate complete specifications for both univariate and multivariate photoperiod models by
# merging the pathogen data frames with the photoperiod model grid.
patuni_photo_df <- expand_grid(patuni_df, mod_photo_df)
patuni_photo_df
patmulti_photo_df <- expand_grid(patmulti_df, mod_photo_df)
patmulti_photo_df
```

# Univariate Models: Generate and Save Model Formulas
```{r}
# For each univariate model:
# - Iterate over unique pathogens in 'patuni_photo_df'.
# - For each pathogen, generate formulas using fun_formulas and aggregate them with fun_add_formula.
# - Save the resulting list of formulas as an RDS file for later model fitting.
patuni_photo_formula_l <- sapply(unique(patuni_photo_df$pat), function(x) {
  l_formula <- list()
  for (i in which(patuni_photo_df$pat == x)) {
    l_formula <- fun_formula_add(
      l_formula, fun_formula(
        pathogen = patuni_photo_df[i,"pat"][[1]], 
        cens = if_else(x == "rota", FALSE, TRUE),
        data = "s08", 
        doses = patuni_photo_df[i,"doses"][[1]], 
        model_nm = patuni_photo_df[i,"model_nm"][[1]], 
        others = patuni_photo_df[i,"others"][[1]][[1]],
        varname = patuni_photo_df[i,"varname"][[1]]))}
  return(l_formula)
}, simplify = FALSE)
```

# Multivariate Models: Generate and Save Model Formulas
```{r}
# For each multivariate model:
# - Iterate over unique pathogens in 'patmulti_photo_df'.
# - Use fun_formulas_multipathogen to generate and aggregate the formulas for each pathogen.
# - Save the resulting list of formulas as an RDS file.
patmulti_photo_formula_l <- sapply(unique(patmulti_photo_df$pat), function(x) {
  l_formula <- list()
  for (i in which(patmulti_photo_df$pat == x)) {
    l_formula <- fun_formula_add(
      l_formula, fun_formula_multipathogen(
        pathogen = patmulti_photo_df[i,"pat"][[1]], 
        data = "s08", 
        doses = patmulti_photo_df[i,"doses"][[1]], 
        model_nm = patmulti_photo_df[i,"model_nm"][[1]], 
        others = patmulti_photo_df[i,"others"][[1]][[1]],
        varname = patmulti_photo_df[i,"varname"][[1]],
        multi_pat = patmulti_photo_df[i,"multi_pat"][[1]][[1]]
        ))}
  return(l_formula)
}, simplify = FALSE)
```

# Sensitivity methods ==============================================================================
```{r}
patuni_photo_df_semeth <- patuni_photo_df %>%
  filter(pat %in% c("mumps", "vzv", "dipht", "mena", "menc", "meny",
                    "strep01", "strep03", "strep04", "strep05", "strep06a", "strep06b", "strep07f", 
                    "strep09v", "strep14", "strep18c", "strep19a", "strep19f", "strep23f")) %>%
  # Fix that dipht only has two vac_conc-vac_name_v1
  mutate(others = case_when(pat == "dipht" ~ list(
    c("vac_conc", "(1|study)", "(1|study:country:center:rct_group)")),
    .default = others))

for (x in unique(patuni_photo_df_semeth$pat)) {
  for (i in which(patuni_photo_df_semeth$pat == x)) {
    patuni_photo_formula_l[[x]] <- fun_formula_add(omit_exp = TRUE,
      patuni_photo_formula_l[[x]], fun_formula(
        pathogen = patuni_photo_df_semeth[i,"pat"][[1]], 
        data = "semeth_s08", 
        doses = patuni_photo_df_semeth[i,"doses"][[1]], 
        model_nm = patuni_photo_df_semeth[i,"model_nm"][[1]], 
        others = patuni_photo_df_semeth[i,"others"][[1]][[1]],
        varname = patuni_photo_df_semeth[i,"varname"][[1]]))
    }
}

patmulti_photo_df_semeth <- patmulti_photo_df %>%
  filter(pat %in% c("multi_men", "multi_strep7", "multi_strep10", "multi_strep11", "multi_strep13")) 

for (x in unique(patmulti_photo_df_semeth$pat)) {
  for (i in which(patmulti_photo_df_semeth$pat == x)) {
    patmulti_photo_formula_l[[x]] <- fun_formula_add(omit_exp = TRUE,
      patmulti_photo_formula_l[[x]], fun_formula_multipathogen(
        pathogen = patmulti_photo_df_semeth[i,"pat"][[1]], 
        data = "semeth_s08", 
        doses = patmulti_photo_df_semeth[i,"doses"][[1]], 
        model_nm = patmulti_photo_df_semeth[i,"model_nm"][[1]], 
        others = patmulti_photo_df_semeth[i,"others"][[1]][[1]],
        varname = patmulti_photo_df_semeth[i,"varname"][[1]],
        multi_pat = patmulti_photo_df_semeth[i,"multi_pat"][[1]][[1]]))
    }
}
```

# Save them ========================================================================================
```{r}
walk(names(patuni_photo_formula_l), function(x) {
  saveRDS(patuni_photo_formula_l[[x]], glue("{dirs$modfit}/formula_brms_{x}_l.rds"))
})
walk(names(patmulti_photo_formula_l), function(x) {
  saveRDS(patmulti_photo_formula_l[[x]], glue("{dirs$modfit}/formula_brms_{x}_l.rds"))
})
```
